title: Four Indian Women Cricketers Sign for WCPL 2026 as Vastrakar Eyes T20 Comeback
excerpt: Pooja Vastrakar, Kiran Navgire, Yastika Bhatia and Shikha Pandey confirmed for Caribbean Premier League starting September 5
body:
• Pooja Vastrakar, Kiran Navgire, Shikha Pandey and Yastika Bhatia confirmed as overseas signings for the 2026 Women's Caribbean Premier League, running September 5-17 at Kensington Oval
  • Vastrakar and Navgire join defending champions Barbados Tridents, while Pandey and Bhatia will play for Trinbago Knight Riders alongside South Africa's Marizanne Kapp
  • The tournament marks Vastrakar's return to official T20 cricket after nearly two years out with shoulder surgery and hamstring injuries

Four Indian women cricketers have been confirmed among the overseas signings for the 2026 Women's Caribbean Premier League (WCPL), the tournament organizers announced on Friday.

Fast-bowling all-rounder Pooja Vastrakar, explosive batter Kiran Navgire, experienced pacer Shikha Pandey, and wicketkeeper-batter Yastika Bhatia will represent two of the four franchises when the competition takes place from September 5-17 at the Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados.

Team Assignments

Vastrakar and Navgire will turn out for defending champions Barbados Tridents. The Indian duo joins former New Zealand batting stalwart Suzie Bates and fellow White Fern Madeline Green as the Tridents' four overseas players.

Pandey, who has played in the previous two WCPL seasons, will be joined by Bhatia at the Trinbago Knight Riders. The pair will feature alongside South Africa's star seam-bowling all-rounder Marizanne Kapp and Australia duo Laura Harris and leg-spinner Madeline Penna.

Apart from Pandey, the other three Indians will be making their WCPL debuts.

Vastrakar's Comeback

The WCPL represents a significant milestone for Vastrakar, who has not played an official T20 international since the 2024 Women's T20 World Cup in October. Shoulder surgery and a subsequent hamstring injury sidelined the Madhya Pradesh all-rounder for an extended period.

Vastrakar returned to competitive action through WPL 2026, playing for eventual champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru, and more recently led Chambal Ghariyals Women to the Madhya Pradesh Women's T20 League title. Her previous overseas franchise cricket experience came via a stint with Brisbane Heat in the 2022-23 WBBL in Australia.

"For Vastrakar, the tournament will mark a return to official T20 cricket after a long injury layoff."

— ESPNcricinfo

Star-Studded Overseas Lineup

The WCPL's overseas signings extend well beyond the Indian contingent. Australia's Meg Lanning headlines the newly formed Jamaica Empress franchise, making her WCPL debut at 34. The former Australian captain is joined by Northern Ireland's Amy Hunter, South Africa's Nonkululeko Mlaba, Pakistan's 22-year-old legspinner Syeda Aroob Shah, and New Zealand's Rosemary Mair.

Guyana Amazon Warriors have assembled a South African-heavy lineup with Shabnim Ismail, Chloe Tryon, Tazmin Brits, and Nadine de Klerk, alongside Australia's 38-year-old all-rounder Erin Burns. Ismail, Burns, and Tryon return to the franchise after missing the 2025 season.

Tournament Format

The 2026 WCPL expands to four teams with the addition of Jamaica Empress. All matches will be played at the Kensington Oval, with the top team in the group stage advancing directly to the final while the second and third-placed teams contest a playoff for the remaining final spot.

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, the growing presence of Indian women in global T20 franchise leagues reflects the expanding footprint of the women's game. With four Indians across two franchises, the WCPL offers another window into the talent pipeline that feeds India's growing ambitions in women's cricket.

Looking Ahead

Navgire, who represents UP Warriorz in the WPL, will gain her first overseas T20 franchise cricket experience through the Caribbean tournament. For Bhatia, the WCPL provides match time ahead of a busy international calendar. Pandey's return for a third consecutive season underlines her value as a reliable overseas performer in Caribbean conditions.
